author: e. m. conner
title: Rounds questions HHS Secretary Kennedy on oversight of lab-grown meat products
text:
U.S. Senator Mike Rounds questioned Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. about the regulation of lab-grown “meat” products during a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on April 22.
The discussion focused on the health and safety concerns related to ultra-processed, cell-cultivated products that are marketed as meat in grocery stores. The topic is important as these new food technologies enter the U.S. market, raising questions about consumer safety and regulatory oversight.
“Throughout your first year in office, you have made ‘Making America Healthy Again’ and eating ‘real food’ a priority,” Rounds said to Kennedy during the hearing. “South Dakota farmers and ranchers work tirelessly to produce some of the safest and highest quality products in the world. I have concerns regarding lab-grown cells, or cell-cultivated products, attempting to enter the US food system posing as meat.” He further asked if Kennedy shared his concerns with these “ultra-processed, lab-grown fake meat products” and how HHS was monitoring their health impacts through FDA oversight.
Kennedy responded: “I share your concern, Senator. I probably have amplified concern. We’re going to exercise FDA’s oversight of them. They’re going to have to show us, they’re going to have to get through a lot of skepticism to show that they’re safe.” The exchange also included examples such as pork fat cells grown in labs combined with plant protein being sold as “meatballs” at grocery stores.
Rounds has served two terms as governor of South Dakota before becoming senator according to his official website. He grew up in Huron, South Dakota, as the eldest of eleven children according to his official website, earned a bachelor’s degree in political science from South Dakota State University according to his official website, and serves on several Senate committees including Appropriations; Armed Services; Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs; Indian Affairs; and Intelligence according to his official website.
The broader implications include increased scrutiny over new food technologies entering American markets while ensuring consumer safety remains a top priority for both lawmakers and federal agencies.
